event.title: G7 Nations to Release 100 Million Barrels of Diesel and Crude Oil
event.canonical_title: G7 Nations to Release 100 Million Barrels of Diesel and Crude Oil
event.summary: In response to rising fuel prices, G7 countries have agreed to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude oil from their strategic reserves. This decision follows a request from the US for European nations to ease the pressure on fuel prices. The release will begin immediately and is expected to be frontloaded over the next four months.

event_overview.title: About Energy Reserves
event_overview.subject: Energy Reserves
event_overview.summary: This event concerns a G7-coordinated emergency drawdown of oil reserves, to be implemented through the International Energy Agency (IEA), in response to oil-market volatility and pressure on diesel supply. On October 2, 2026, G7 leaders said 100 million barrels would be released over four months, with a substantial diesel component front-loaded in the first 20 days; the action builds on the IEA’s broader March 2026 emergency response to Middle East supply disruptions.

facts.label: Announcement and schedule
facts.value: G7 leaders met virtually on October 2, 2026 and said the coordinated 100-million-barrel release would begin immediately and run for four months, including an early diesel release by G7 members and partners.

facts.label: Coordinating framework
facts.value: The release is to be coordinated through the IEA. Under the Agreement on an International Energy Programme, IEA countries must hold oil stocks equivalent to at least 90 days of net oil imports and be prepared to respond collectively to severe supply disruptions.

facts.label: Purpose and limits
facts.value: The IEA emergency-response system is intended to mitigate the economic effects of sudden, short-term oil supply shortages by adding supply or restraining demand; the IEA says it is not a tool for price intervention or long-term supply management.

facts.label: What can be released
facts.value: Emergency holdings may be crude oil or refined products and may be held by governments, specialised agencies, or obligated industry. National governments retain authority over releases from those systems.

facts.label: Related 2026 action
facts.value: The IEA’s sixth and largest collective action was announced on March 11, 2026; by March 19, the agency reported that member-country contributions totalled 426 million barrels, primarily crude oil but with refined-product contributions concentrated in Europe.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the October 2-3, 2026 G7 announcement and immediate framing of the reserve release, not the full March 2026 IEA action, country-by-country allocations, individual sales, or subsequent market effects.
